t:
The Secretary of the Air Force shall ensure that the next-generation long-range strike bomber is—
    (1) capable of carrying strategic nuclear weapons as of the date on which such aircraft achieves initial operating capability; and 
    (2) certified to use such weapons by not later than two years after such date.

fable.w: This section directs a federal official to ensure a bomber is nuclear-capable and certified by a deadline; it is a purely internal federal directive. One might read "certified" as implying some procedural process, but no outside party (states, public, experts, industry) is consulted or given any role, and no rulemaking, hearing, or right to sue is created.

opus.w: The section only directs the Secretary of the Air Force to make sure the next-generation bomber can carry nuclear weapons and is certified to use them by a deadline. It requires no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with states or other outside entities, or right to sue. A reader might take 'certified' as a sign of outside review, but certification here is an internal federal military process.

qwen_chat.w: The section mandates that the Secretary of the Air Force ensure the bomber is capable of carrying nuclear weapons and is certified to use them. All actors involved (the Secretary, the Air Force) are inside the federal government. There is no requirement for consultation, coordination, or participation by any outside party (such as the public, states, tribes, or independent experts) in making these decisions. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "certified" implies a process involving outside experts or agencies, but the text does not specify who performs the certification or if any outside party is involved. The actors mentioned are the Secretary of the Air Force (federal) and the aircraft itself. There is no mention of consultation, public comment, advisory boards with non-federal members, or coordination with states/tribes/public. The entire process described is internal to the Department of the Air Force.
